detail.scope: Commercial-sector electricity sales and average price by state, as reported to EIA. Data centers are billed mostly in the commercial class, so this is a proxy for their load, not a measurement of it.

sources.name: ERCOT
sources.scope: Large generators with a full interconnection study requested, from the monthly Generator Interconnection Status report for Texas. Includes projects from study through commissioning.

sources.name: NYISO
sources.scope: Projects in the New York interconnection queue as NYISO publishes them.

sources.name: MISO
sources.scope: Projects in the Midcontinent generator interconnection queue, all statuses as MISO publishes them.

sources.name: Southwest Power Pool
sources.scope: Generator interconnection requests across the south-central US, all statuses as SPP publishes them, withdrawn requests counted separately.

sources.name: CAISO
sources.scope: Active generator interconnection requests on the California ISO grid, from the public queue report. Completed and withdrawn projects are counted separately.

analysis.body:
In June 2026, commercial-sector electricity sales across the eight states listed totaled 54,797.55 MWh. Texas led with 15,753.83 MWh and California followed with 10,024.68 MWh, while Oregon was lowest at 2,216.05 MWh. Average commercial prices ranged from $8.66 per MWh in Texas to $27.33 per MWh in California, with Virginia at $10.99 and Georgia at $11.91. Because data centers are billed mostly in the commercial class, these figures are a proxy for data center load, not a direct measurement.

The interconnection queues show planned generation and storage waiting to connect, not data center demand itself. ERCOT lists 438,086.5 MW, NYISO 319,115.45 MW, MISO 299,720.6 MW, SPP 198,074.27 MW, and CAISO 71,308.82 MW. Storage is the largest category in ERCOT at 159,820.34 MW and in CAISO at 46,570.26 MW, and it is second in MISO at 67,026.89 MW and SPP at 52,513.09 MW. Gas queue capacity is 78,092.4 MW in ERCOT, 27,879 MW in NYISO, 30,236.33 MW in MISO, 47,221.675 MW in SPP, and 915.6 MW in CAISO. Storage and gas growth track data center load, but these are supply-side projects, not demand.

The sources are not directly comparable because each operator uses different scope and status definitions. Solar queue capacity is 150,347.17 MW in ERCOT, 146,004.28 MW in MISO, 33,533.665 MW in SPP, 18,896.074 MW in CAISO, and 80 MW in NYISO. Wind queue capacity is 48,182.96 MW in ERCOT, 52,046.42 MW in MISO, 64,658.84 MW in SPP, and 4,575.184 MW in CAISO. The EIA commercial sales cover only eight states and one month, so they cannot be compared directly to these queue totals. Watch next whether the 159,820.34 MW of storage in ERCOT and 67,026.89 MW in MISO move from queue to operation, since that conversion would indicate supply responding to data center load.
